Had Better for What Is Advisable
You use had better to share ideas with others regarding what you believe is the best action to take in a specific situation.

When you use had better, you are trying to give a recommendation about a present situation in which you are telling another person what to do. The use of had better suggests that if the other person does not follow what you propose, a bad consequence will happen.

To make sentences using had better, you have to follow the structure:

Subject + had better + verb (base form) + complement.

For example,
You had better check that the code is correctly written.
The university had better teach its students how to write codes.

Remember that you can also use the abbreviation of the expression had better which is ‘d better.
Indeed, you'd better study thoroughly as the teacher might want to get full answers on all term's topics.
Now, you'd better memorize all of that before you present the exam as not many students really prepare for it.
You use quantifiers to enunciate the quantity or amount of something.

The negative form of the quantifier many needs a countable noun right after the expression. It implies the idea that something is not frequently seen or done.

Examples:
Not many people know about coding and Java.
Not many codes are easily understandable.
Not many software technicians specialize on Java.
I heard that not many students tend to pass it.
Now, you'd better memorize all of that before you present the exam as not many students really prepare for it.

images.text:
Diego: I'm a bit nervous about tomorrow's exam. I heard that not many students tend to pass it.
Tara: Well, I was one of the few that passed it last year. Indeed, you'd better study thoroughly as the teacher might want to get full answers on all term's topics. One of the topics that not many students check is the syntax in integer data types; so, what can you tell me about that?
Diego: The integer, which contains the short, int, and long data types, presents numeric values that are whole values, large numbers. Now, the variable declaration of these data types follows a specific syntax in which we assign a value to the variable. In other words, you might want to code something like variable type variable name = 15;

Tara: Correct. You also ought to make an in-depth review of short data types.
Diego: Let me see. The short data type is the smallest one. Plus, it takes 2 bytes of memory which is the same as 16 bits. It also shares the characteristic of accepting negative as well as positive values, just like the int and long data types do. Moreover, its default value is zero and you ought to only introduce values within the range of -32,768 to 32,767.

Tara: Great! You might want to also check the int and long data types…
Diego: Okay, I'd better recall that the int type consumes 32 bits of memory and that it takes values from -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647. Regarding the long one, it takes 64 bits of memory and you ought to introduce values from -9,223,372,036,854,775,808 to -9,223,372,036,854,775,807.
Tara: Now, you'd better memorize all of that before you present the exam as not many students really prepare for it. Don't forget, you ought to pass that exam!
